children: U.S. factory orders rose in July, exceeding expectations after two months of declines, the Census Bureau said Wednesday.
Orders from U.S. factories jumped 0.9% in July to $663.6 billion from $657.8 billion in June. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a 0.7% increase.

The report showed that shipments from factories increased 0.8% in July after being virtually unchanged month-over-month in June. Unfilled orders rose 0.6% and have now risen 24 of the past 25 months, the report said.
